title: THE SAME GOD FOR EVERY WORSHIPPER

memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "'When you prepare a young bull as a burnt offering or sacrifice, for a special vow or a fellowship offering to the Lord, bring with the bull a grain offering of three-tenths of an ephah of the finest flour mixed with half a hin of olive oil. Also bring half a hin of wine as a drink offering. It will be a food offering, an aroma pleasing to the Lord. Each one of you must do these things in this way when you present a food offering as an aroma pleasing to the Lord.'" — Num 15:8-12 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
God spells out the offerings for a bull, larger than the ram or lamb, with proportionally larger amounts of flour, oil, and wine. There is an order and fairness to it all. The bigger the gift, the fuller the accompanying offering — everything measured, everything fitting.

But the line that stands out is at the end: "Each one of you must do these things in this way." Whether a person brought a small lamb or a large bull, the same principles applied to everyone. Rich or poor, prominent or ordinary, all came to God on the same terms. There was one way of worship for all His people.

This points to a truth that runs right through Scripture: God shows no favouritism. He does not have one set of rules for the important and another for the overlooked. The same holy God, approached the same way, by every worshipper. Before Him, all stand on level ground.

How much more is this true in the gospel. There are not different doors into God's presence for different classes of people. Rich and poor, from every nation and background, come to God through the one and only way — Jesus Christ. There is one Mediator, one sacrifice, one open door. Whatever your status in the eyes of the world, you come to God on exactly the same terms as everyone else: through faith in His Son. That is humbling for the proud and wonderfully freeing for the lowly.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Do you ever imagine some people have easier access to God than others?
2. How does it humble you that all come to God on the same terms?
3. How does it comfort you that the one door to God is open to you in Christ?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Father, thank You that You show no favouritism and that all Your people come to You the same way. Thank You that in Christ there is one open door for rich and poor, for every nation and background. Draw me near through Him. Amen.
